title: The King and His Empire

fact_notes: Kalinga war about 261 BCE, in the eighth year after Ashoka's consecration (Rock Edict XIII). Kalinga is roughly modern Odisha, on the east coast.
Rock Edict XIII (trans. S. Dhammika): 'One hundred and fifty thousand were deported, one hundred thousand were killed and many more died.'

Rock Edict XIII (trans. S. Dhammika): 'Indeed, the Beloved-of-the-Gods is deeply pained by the killing, dying and deportation that take place when an unconquered country is conquered.' Ashoka calls himself Devanampiya, Beloved of the Gods.
Ashoka (r. c. 268-232 BCE), capital Pataliputra (modern Patna); grandson of Chandragupta Maurya, founder of the Maurya Empire.
Extent: inscriptions from Kandahar (Afghanistan) to the east; commonly cited as Afghanistan to Bengal.
Edicts in Prakrit (Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts); Greek and Aramaic at Kandahar.
Rock Edict II: medical treatment for humans and animals, wells dug, trees planted. Pillar Edict VII: rest houses and wells along roads.
Dhamma: Ashoka's moral teaching; edicts urge kindness, truthfulness and respect for all sects (Rock Edict XII).
Lion Capital of Ashoka, Sarnath, adopted as the State Emblem of India on 26 January 1950; about 2,200 years after Ashoka (twenty-two centuries).
The Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes) at the centre of India's flag is taken from the wheel on Ashoka's capitals.
